done_when: In the generated CI workflow, a failed uv install step tries once more by itself before the job fails

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a transient uv installation failure in the trusted review or nightly job.
Both tests use `_assert_retry`, which checks only that the retry condition contains a particular substring. Appending `&& github.event_name == 'pull_request'` would still pass both tests, while disabling retries for `pull_request_target`, scheduled and manual runs. The helper also counts three pairs without checking which jobs contain them, so moving the nightly pair into another job would pass. Conversely, wrapping the equivalent condition in `${{ ... }}`, which [GitHub Actions accepts](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idstepsif), breaks the test. Check the effective condition and its job at the generated-workflow boundary.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_new_repo_retries_uv_install_once and test_2_earlier_adopted_repo_gets_uv_retry_on_sync

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - an earlier-adopted client syncs its existing CI workflow after upgrading Forge.
The copied v1.2.2 fixture has no `.github/workflows/forge.yml`, and the seed repo contains only a README (`tests/conftest.py:475-479`). This test therefore checks creation, not replacement, of the workflow. A regression that creates missing workflows but leaves existing ones unchanged would pass, while existing clients retain the single-attempt install. Start this case with the earlier generated workflow and verify that sync replaces it.
findings.title: Gate: test_2_earlier_adopted_repo_gets_uv_retry_on_sync

stop.reason: The owner wants one more round to make both tests stronger

why: The CI step that installs uv fails often on a GitHub server error, and each failure needs a manual rerun
